correctness.rationale: For a finite commutative unital ring, simultaneous residue reduction modulo the distinct maximal ideals is surjective with kernel J. An irredundant unit-ideal generating family has one private nonzero coordinate per member. On the fixed vertex's co-support C, subtract the choices with no all-zero partner column from all partner residue assignments. On C^c, start with all nonzero partner columns; forbidding private coordinates for a designated set of a partners removes a(q_i-1) singleton columns at coordinate i. Inclusion–exclusion on those designated partners gives exactly the stated degree, with j^(k-1) lifts and a (k-1)! ordering divisor. Private coordinates ensure distinct members and rule out both units and radical elements, and |C^c|<k-1 gives zero. For Boolean triples, writing s=n-t, the degree is (4^s-3^s)(3^t-2^(t+1)+1)/2. The t=1 degree is zero. For t>=5, 3^(t-1)/2^(t+1)>1 (already 81/64 at t=5 and increasing), so B_t<4B_(t-1) while A_(s+1)>4A_s; such t lose. The remaining t=2,3,4 multipliers are 1,6,25. For n>=5, t=3 strictly beats t=2 since A_(s+1)/A_s decreases and is already <6 at s=2. The t=4 class beats t=3 exactly when (4/3)^(n-4)>7, which holds from n=11 without an integer tie. Checking the admissible t for n=3,4 gives degrees 1,7, respectively. Independent integer evaluation of the formula yields the stated n=10 and n=11 maxima and the runner-up at n=11. RESULT.md §§1–4 and the finite enumeration in verify.py and verification_output.txt were inspected; the packaged script was not executed, and the finite checks are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: Incidence degree is a natural local invariant missing from total-edge enumerations; a fixed-vertex formula works even for unequal residue sizes and nontrivial radical fibres. Rank three is the first hypergraph case beyond graphs, and its finite crossover to a different stable maximum-degree stratum is a precise extremal result for an entire natural family, not a choice of a single numerical ring.
